root_cause_label: Literal Account-Number Grep Misses Typo Variants of Account Numbers
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent correctly identified the company via name-based grep and extracted known account numbers, but applied only exact-match filtering on those numbers, missing any records where the account number itself is a typo variant not reachable from an initial name match.
t_err_evidence: In step 4 the agent resolves all relevant account numbers (BUS-30001, BUS-30999, BUS-35001) solely from a literal name grep, then in step 5 filters by those exact strings — no consideration is given to fuzzy variants of the account numbers, so records with typo account numbers that share no name match with 'North West Capital' are silently excluded.
t_commit_evidence: In step 6 the agent writes /app/data/output.json using the fixed set of three account numbers; once the file is written and the agent declares 'task complete', the erroneous result is locked in.
trigger_explanation: The agent assumes that all account numbers for the target company can be discovered through a literal name grep, and that exact account-number matching on those discovered numbers is sufficient. It never considers that some records may have typo account numbers that would not surface in the name grep (e.g., BUS-3g001 instead of BUS-30001), so it acts on this unverified assumption throughout the solution.
forewarning_evidence: Step 4 output contains 'BUS-30999' attributed to the typo company name ('North West Capital Group Incoporated'), which should signal that account numbers themselves can be garbled; the agent notes the name typo but does not reason about whether BUS-30999 is itself a typo of BUS-30001 or whether other typo account numbers might exist in records with no name match.
